public_rationale: Under the post's six-to-twelve-month context, the prediction is supported. Research published before the one-year deadline documented substantial errors in leading assistants even with access to sources. The contemporary scientific assessment also found unresolved reliability problems. Legal RAG evaluations showed meaningful improvements, but continuing hallucinations. This supports the prediction that a broad solution was not imminent; it does not establish that RAG is useless or that a new architecture is necessary.
limitations: The one-year deadline is a contextual interpretation of near at hand.
The BBC's 51% measure includes issues beyond factual errors and should not be described as a hallucination rate.
The principal late-period tests concern December 2024 systems, not every system on 2025-02-23.
The evidence supports a practical assessment of unresolved reliability, not proof that no private or specialized solution existed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: A solution to AI unreliability and hallucination is not near at hand.

statement.excerpt: But we are kidding ourselves if it we think the solution is near at hand.
statement.document_title: No, RAG is probably not going to rescue the current situation

from_speaker: perfectly reliable, hallucination-free chatbots by this time next year
our_interpretation: The solution means resolving the broad factual unreliability and hallucination problem discussed in the post.
I interpret near at hand using the surrounding six-month and one-year statements, with the latest deadline being 2025-02-23.
The ordinary reading predicts that broadly trustworthy chatbots will not arrive within that interval. It does not predict that reliability will fail to improve.
Evidence of frequent material errors can support this reading without requiring a philosophical proof that error-free software is impossible.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations during the stated near-term interval, including evidence near its end, show that leading general-purpose or retrieval-enabled systems still make substantial factual errors and that no broadly validated solution has emerged.
criteria.contradiction_condition: By 2025-02-23, an available system or method demonstrably resolves broad chatbot unreliability, supported by independent evaluations across varied factual and reasoning tasks and realistic use.

evidence.explanation: The BBC tested ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini and Perplexity with access to BBC sources. Beyond the broader issue measure quoted here, it reported factual errors in 19% of answers citing BBC content, supporting continued factual unreliability.

evidence.excerpt: Existing guardrails to contain and mitigate reliability issues are not fail-proof.
evidence.explanation: The scientific review reports continuing reliability problems and limitations in methods for mitigating hallucinations. The event date uses its stated writing cutoff rather than treating January publication as a new experiment.

The study found that legal RAG tools reduced hallucinations relative to GPT-4, while still producing substantial errors. This qualifies any suggestion that RAG offered no benefit, but does not demonstrate a general solution.
